items.question: In the emergency procedures definitions, what does 'Land Immediately' mean?
options: Land at the next scheduled destination
Land on the nearest clear area where a safe normal landing can be performed
Land at the nearest airport only
Descend to a lower altitude and continue flight
items.explanation: The DEFINITIONS section defines 'Land Immediately' as landing on the nearest clear area where a safe normal landing can be performed, being prepared to enter autorotation.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: DEFINITIONS (p.3-1)

items.question: What does 'Land as soon as practical' mean in the emergency procedures definitions?
options: Continue flight to home base
Land at pilot's discretion, but flight beyond the nearest airport is not recommended
Land only if a warning light is accompanied by other indications
Descend to 500 ft AGL and reassess
items.explanation: 'Land as soon as practical' is defined as landing site at pilot's discretion based on the nature of the problem, with flight beyond the nearest airport not recommended.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: DEFINITIONS (p.3-1)

items.question: In the POWER FAILURE - GENERAL description, which event usually indicates a power failure?
options: Illumination of the LOW FUEL light
Illumination of the LOW RPM horn
Activation of the ALT warning light
Loss of hydraulic pressure
items.explanation: The general power failure discussion states that a power failure will usually be indicated by the low RPM horn.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: Which of the following may indicate an engine failure according to the POWER FAILURE - GENERAL section?
options: Nose right yaw and increasing rotor RPM
Change in noise level, nose left yaw, an oil pressure light, or decreasing engine RPM
AUX FUEL PUMP light with no other indications
Increase in manifold pressure at constant power
items.explanation: Engine failure indications include change in noise level, nose left yaw, an oil pressure light, or decreasing engine RPM.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: According to POWER FAILURE - GENERAL, what is the immediate pilot action in case of power failure?
options: Raise collective to maintain altitude
Lower collective to enter autorotation and reduce airspeed to power-off Vne or below
Turn towards the nearest airport before adjusting collective
Increase throttle and climb
items.explanation: The procedure states that in case of power failure, immediately lower collective to enter autorotation and reduce airspeed to power-off Vne or below.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: In the CAUTION under POWER FAILURE - GENERAL, what cyclic input is required when lowering collective at high airspeed?
options: Left cyclic
Right cyclic
Forward cyclic
Aft cyclic
items.explanation: A caution notes that aft cyclic is required when collective is lowered at high airspeed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: According to the CAUTION at the end of POWER FAILURE - GENERAL, why should aft cyclic not be applied during touchdown or ground slide?
options: It may reduce rotor RPM below limits
It may cause excessive nose-up attitude and tail skid
It may cause possible blade strike to tailcone
It may cause loss of tail rotor effectiveness
items.explanation: The caution warns not to apply aft cyclic during touchdown or ground slide to prevent possible blade strike to tailcone.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: In a power failure above 500 feet AGL, what is the recommended airspeed for the steady glide?
options: 55 KIAS
60 KIAS
70 KIAS
80 KIAS
items.explanation: The POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL procedure specifies establishing a steady glide at approximately 70 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: For a power failure above 500 feet AGL, what rotor RPM range should be maintained during the glide?
items.explanation: The procedure calls for adjusting collective to keep RPM between 97 and 108%, or full down if light weight prevents attaining above 97%.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: During a power failure above 500 feet AGL, at approximately what height should the pilot begin the cyclic flare?
options: 20 feet AGL
30 feet AGL
40 feet AGL
60 feet AGL
items.explanation: The procedure directs the pilot to begin cyclic flare at about 40 feet AGL to reduce rate of descent and forward speed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: In a power failure between 8 feet and 500 feet AGL, what is the first action?
options: Apply forward cyclic
Lower collective immediately to maintain rotor RPM
Roll throttle off into overtravel spring
Select a landing spot into wind
items.explanation: The POWER FAILURE BETWEEN 8 FEET AND 500 FEET AGL procedure starts with lowering collective immediately to maintain rotor RPM.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE BETWEEN 8 FEET AND 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: For a power failure between 8 feet and 500 feet AGL, what is the recommended action as the ground is approached?
options: Increase airspeed and delay the flare
Begin cyclic flare to reduce rate of descent and forward speed
Apply full aft cyclic at 20 feet
Lower collective to full down
items.explanation: The procedure states that as the ground is approached, begin cyclic flare to reduce rate of descent and forward speed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE BETWEEN 8 FEET AND 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: In the POWER FAILURE BELOW 8 FEET AGL procedure, which pedal input is required to prevent yawing?
options: Left pedal
Right pedal
No pedal input is used
Pedals are centered
items.explanation: The procedure specifies applying right pedal as required to prevent yawing.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE BELOW 8 FEET AGL (p.3-3)

items.question: For maximum glide distance configuration, what airspeed is recommended?
options: 55 KIAS
60 KIAS
70 KIAS
90 KIAS
items.explanation: The MAXIMUM GLIDE DISTANCE CONFIGURATION recommends approximately 90 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: MAXIMUM GLIDE DISTANCE CONFIGURATION (p.3-3)

items.question: For minimum rate of descent configuration in autorotation, what airspeed is recommended?
options: 45 KIAS
55 KIAS
65 KIAS
75 KIAS
items.explanation: The MINIMUM RATE OF DESCENT CONFIGURATION recommends approximately 55 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: MINIMUM RATE OF DESCENT CONFIGURATION (p.3-3)

items.question: According to the AIR RESTART PROCEDURE, what is the first step before engaging the starter?
options: Mixture - Off
Fuel valve - On
Battery switch - On
Throttle - Closed
items.explanation: The AIR RESTART PROCEDURE lists 'Mixture - Off' as the first step before closing the throttle and engaging the starter.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AIR RESTART PROCEDURE (p.3-3)

items.question: In the AIR RESTART PROCEDURE, when should the mixture be moved slowly rich?
options: Before the starter is engaged
While cranking with the starter engaged
After reaching 70 KIAS
After landing
items.explanation: The procedure states 'Mixture - move slowly rich while cranking', meaning during starter engagement.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AIR RESTART PROCEDURE (p.3-3)

items.question: What caution is given before attempting an air restart in flight?
options: Do not attempt restart above 5000 feet AGL
Do not attempt restart if engine malfunction is suspected or before safe autorotation is established
Do not attempt restart with passengers on board
Do not attempt restart with any warning light illuminated
items.explanation: The caution states not to attempt restart if engine malfunction is suspected or before safe autorotation is established; air restarts are not recommended below 2000 feet AGL.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AIR RESTART PROCEDURE (p.3-3)

items.question: During an EMERGENCY WATER LANDING - POWER OFF, what action should be taken as the aircraft contacts the water?
options: Apply full aft cyclic
Apply lateral cyclic to stop the rotors
Raise collective to climb away
Roll throttle to full open
items.explanation: The POWER OFF water landing procedure directs the pilot to apply lateral cyclic when the aircraft contacts the water to stop the rotors.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: EMERGENCY WATER LANDING - POWER OFF (p.3-4)

items.question: Before an EMERGENCY WATER LANDING - POWER OFF, what cockpit action is recommended if time permits?
options: Turn battery and alternator OFF
Unlatch doors prior to water contact
Switch fuel valve OFF
Apply rotor brake
items.explanation: The procedure advises unlatching doors prior to water contact if time permits.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: EMERGENCY WATER LANDING - POWER OFF (p.3-4)

items.question: In an EMERGENCY WATER LANDING - POWER ON, what should passengers do before the pilot shuts down the helicopter on the water?
options: Secure seat belts and remain seated
Exit the aircraft while it is hovering over the water
Move to the front seats
Deploy life rafts from the baggage compartment
items.explanation: The POWER ON water landing procedure directs that passengers exit the aircraft while it is hovering over the water before the pilot shuts down.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: EMERGENCY WATER LANDING - POWER ON (p.3-4)

items.question: For LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT, what is the first required pilot action?
options: Reduce airspeed to 60 KIAS
Immediately enter autorotation
Roll throttle off into overtravel spring while maintaining power
Apply full left pedal and climb
items.explanation: The LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT procedure begins with immediately entering autorotation.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT (p.3-5)

items.question: When experiencing LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT and a suitable landing site is not immediately available, what does the note say about limited controlled flight?
options: Limited control is possible at any airspeed with full power
Vertical stabilizers may permit limited controlled flight at low power settings and airspeeds above 70 KIAS
Controlled flight is not possible and immediate landing is required
Limited control is only possible below 40 KIAS
items.explanation: The note states that the vertical stabilizers may permit limited controlled flight at low power settings and airspeeds above 70 KIAS; however, prior to reducing airspeed, enter full autorotation.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT (p.3-5)

items.question: In LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN HOVER, what should the pilot do immediately when failure is indicated by nose right yaw that cannot be stopped?
options: Apply full left pedal and increase power
Immediately roll throttle off into overtravel spring and allow the aircraft to settle
Push cyclic forward and climb
Lower collective to down stop and accelerate
items.explanation: The hover tail rotor failure procedure specifies immediately rolling throttle off into overtravel spring and allowing the aircraft to settle.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN HOVER (p.3-5)

items.question: What is the required action if ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND occurs and the engine starts?
options: Shut down immediately and evacuate
Run the engine at 60-70% RPM for a short time
Increase RPM to 100% and take off
Turn battery switch OFF and continue cranking
items.explanation: For an engine fire during start on ground, if the engine starts, the procedure calls for running it at 60-70% RPM for a short time before shutting down.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND (p.3-6)

items.question: In ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND, which two fuel-related controls must be moved to OFF as part of the sequence?
options: Fuel mixture and fuel valve
Fuel valve and carb heat
Mixture and governor switch
Fuel pump and fuel filter
items.explanation: The procedure lists 'Fuel mixture - OFF' and 'Fuel valve - OFF' as steps after attempting to start and running the engine briefly.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND (p.3-6)

items.question: For ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT, what are the first two actions listed?
options: Turn cabin heat OFF and cabin vent ON
Enter autorotation and then turn cabin heat OFF if time permits
Switch battery OFF and then enter autorotation
Roll throttle off and increase airspeed
items.explanation: The ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT procedure begins with 'Enter autorotation' followed by 'Cabin heat - OFF (if time permits)'.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6)

items.question: According to ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT procedures, what is the initial action if an electrical fire is suspected?
options: Open cabin vents
Land immediately
Battery and alternator switches - OFF
Pull all circuit breakers
items.explanation: The first step for electrical fire in flight is to switch battery and alternator OFF.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6)

items.question: When both battery and alternator switches are OFF due to an electrical fire in flight, what important system becomes inoperative according to the note?
options: Fuel pumps
Rotor brake
Hydraulic system
Low RPM warning system and governor
items.explanation: The note states that the low RPM warning system and governor are inoperative with battery and alternator switches both OFF.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6)

items.question: In the TACHOMETER FAILURE procedure, what should the pilot do if it is not clear which tachometer is malfunctioning or if both tachs malfunction?
options: Turn off the governor and continue flight
Allow the governor to control RPM and land as soon as practical
Use manifold pressure only and continue to destination
Descend to 500 feet AGL and troubleshoot
items.explanation: The TACHOMETER FAILURE procedure directs the pilot to allow the governor to control RPM and land as soon as practical if it is not clear which tach is malfunctioning or both tachs malfunction.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: TACHOMETER FAILURE (p.3-7)

items.question: How is a HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAILURE primarily indicated in the R44 II?
options: Loss of LOW RPM horn
Heavy or stiff cyclic and collective controls
Illumination of the HYD warning light only
Sudden increase in engine RPM
items.explanation: The HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAILURE description states that failure is indicated by heavy or stiff cyclic and collective controls, sometimes with intermittent or vibrating feedback.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAILURE (p.3-7)

items.question: In the HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAILURE procedure, what is the correct handling of the HYD switch?
options: Turn HYD switch OFF immediately and leave it OFF
Verify HYD switch ON, and if hydraulics are not restored, set HYD switch OFF
Cycle HYD switch OFF and ON repeatedly
Leave HYD switch in its current position and continue flight
items.explanation: The procedure first calls for verifying HYD switch ON, and if hydraulics are not restored, turning HYD switch OFF, then adjusting airspeed and landing as soon as practical.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAILURE (p.3-7)

items.question: What is the recommended response to a GOVERNOR FAILURE in flight?
options: Turn governor OFF and descend at once
Grip throttle firmly to override the governor, switch governor OFF, and complete the flight using manual throttle control
Reduce to idle and auto-rotate
Turn off alternator and battery
items.explanation: For a governor failure, the POH instructs the pilot to grip the throttle firmly to override the malfunctioning governor, switch the governor OFF, and complete the flight using manual throttle control.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: GOVERNOR FAILURE (p.3-7)

items.question: When the OIL warning light confirms a loss of oil pressure, what action is required?
options: Continue flight to the nearest airport while monitoring gages
Reduce power and continue at a lower airspeed
Land immediately because continued operation without oil pressure may cause engine failure
Pull mixture to idle cut-off and continue autorotation only if RPM decays
items.explanation: The OIL light indicates loss of engine power or oil pressure. If oil pressure loss is confirmed, the POH states to land immediately since continued operation without oil pressure will cause serious engine damage and possible engine failure.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - OIL (p.3-8)

items.question: What does the note for MR CHIP and TR CHIP warning lights require if a chip light comes on again after cleaning and a 30-minute hover?
options: Continue flight and recheck at next inspection
Replace the affected gearbox before further flight
Pull the circuit breaker and continue
Reduce power and continue to destination
items.explanation: The note explains that if no metal chips or slivers are found, the detector may have break-in fuzz; clean and reinstall, hover for at least 30 minutes, and if the chip light comes on again, replace the gearbox before further flight.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - MR CHIP/TR CHIP (p.3-8)

items.question: When the LOW FUEL light illuminates, approximately how long will the engine run at cruise power before fuel exhaustion?
options: 5 minutes
10 minutes
15 minutes
20 minutes
items.explanation: The LOW FUEL light indicates approximately three gallons of usable fuel remaining, and the POH states the engine will run out of fuel after ten minutes at cruise power.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - LOW FUEL (p.3-9)

items.question: For the AUX FUEL PUMP warning light, when is an immediate landing required rather than 'land as soon as practical'?
options: Whenever the light illuminates
Only when accompanied by erratic engine operation
Only when the LOW FUEL light is also on
Whenever the fuel quantity is below 1/4 tank
items.explanation: The POH states that if the AUX FUEL PUMP light is accompanied by erratic engine operation, the pilot should land immediately; otherwise, land as soon as practical.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - AUX FUEL PUMP (p.3-9)

items.question: According to the FUEL FILTER warning light procedure, when must the pilot land immediately?
options: Whenever the FUEL FILTER light illuminates
When the FUEL FILTER light is accompanied by LOW FUEL
When the FUEL FILTER light is accompanied by AUX FUEL PUMP light or erratic engine operation
Only when the fuel pressure drops to zero
items.explanation: The FUEL FILTER light alone requires landing as soon as practical, but if it is accompanied by the AUX FUEL PUMP warning light or erratic engine operation, the POH instructs to land immediately.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - FUEL FILTER (p.3-9)

items.question: If the CLUTCH light comes on in flight and does not go out within about 10 seconds, what action does the POH recommend?
options: Pull CLUTCH circuit breaker and land as soon as practical
Increase power and continue flight
Turn the governor OFF
Ignore the light if there is no vibration
items.explanation: The note for the CLUTCH light states that if it flickers or comes on in flight and does not go out within 10 seconds, the pilot should pull the CLUTCH circuit breaker and land as soon as practical, reducing power and landing immediately if there are other indications of drive system failure.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - CLUTCH (p.3-9)

items.question: What does the ALT warning light indicate and what is the recommended response if it stays on after reset?
options: Low oil temperature; continue flight
Low voltage and possible alternator failure; turn off nonessential electrical equipment and land as soon as practical
Low fuel pump pressure; descend to a lower altitude
High alternator voltage; turn alternator OFF and continue
items.explanation: The ALT light indicates low voltage and possible alternator failure. The POH instructs pilots to turn off nonessential electrical equipment, attempt a reset by switching ALT OFF then ON, and if the light stays on, land as soon as practical because continued flight without a functioning alternator can result in loss of power to the tachometers.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - ALT (p.3-10)

items.question: If the STARTER ON light does not go out when the starter button is released, what immediate action is specified?
options: Reduce throttle to idle and continue cranking
Turn alternator OFF and monitor amps
Immediately pull mixture OFF and turn battery switch OFF
Pull all circuit breakers and continue
items.explanation: For a STARTER ON light that remains illuminated, the POH instructs the pilot to immediately pull mixture OFF and turn the battery switch OFF, then have the starter motor serviced.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - STARTER ON (p.3-10)

items.question: When the LOW RPM warning light illuminates in flight, what control inputs are recommended to restore rotor RPM?
options: Raise collective and apply forward cyclic
Lower collective, roll throttle on, and in forward flight apply aft cyclic
Raise collective and reduce throttle
Lower collective and apply left pedal
items.explanation: The LOW RPM light indicates rotor speed below 97% RPM. The POH directs the pilot to lower collective, roll throttle on, and in forward flight apply aft cyclic to restore RPM; the light is disabled when collective is full down.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - LOW RPM (p.3-10)

items.question: What is the required action when the CARBON MONOXIDE warning light is illuminated and symptoms such as headache, drowsiness, or dizziness appear?
options: Increase cabin heat and continue flight
Open vents but continue if symptoms are mild
Shut off heater, open nose and door vents, and land immediately
Descend to a lower altitude and continue flight
items.explanation: The CARBON MONOXIDE light indicates elevated CO levels. The POH instructs the pilot to shut off the heater and open nose and door vents; if CO poisoning symptoms accompany the light, land immediately.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - CARBON MONOXIDE (p.3-10)

items.question: What does the FULL THROTTLE warning light (if installed) indicate, and how should the pilot respond?
options: Engine is at idle; increase throttle
Engine is near full throttle and the governor cannot increase throttle further; lower collective to extinguish the light
Alternator is overloaded; turn alternator OFF
Hydraulic pressure is low; turn HYD switch OFF
items.explanation: The FULL THROTTLE light indicates the engine is near full throttle so the governor cannot further increase throttle to maintain RPM; the POH states the pilot should lower collective as required to extinguish the light.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS - FULL THROTTLE (p.3-10)

items.question: What does the HIGH RPM WARBLE audio alert indicate and what is the correct pilot response?
options: Rotor speed is below 97% RPM; lower collective and roll throttle on
Rotor speed is approaching the 108% RPM limit; raise collective as required to control RPM
Engine RPM is below idle; increase throttle to restore RPM
Tail rotor RPM is low; apply right pedal
items.explanation: The HIGH RPM WARBLE is a high/low tone in the audio system which indicates rotor speed is approaching the 108% RPM limit; the POH instructs the pilot to raise collective as required to control RPM.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AUDIO ALERTS - HIGH RPM WARBLE (p.3-11)

items.question: If headset audio fails in flight, what does the POH require?
options: Continue flight and monitor instruments closely
Land as soon as practical
Land immediately
Descend below 500 feet AGL and troubleshoot
items.explanation: The HEADSET AUDIO FAILURE procedure states that if headset audio fails, the pilot should land as soon as practical.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: HEADSET AUDIO FAILURE (p.3-5)

items.question: What important caution is associated with headset audio failure on aircraft where the low RPM horn is provided through the audio system?
options: The LOW FUEL light will not illuminate
The alternator will not charge the battery
The pilot will not hear the low RPM horn
The hydraulic system will switch off
items.explanation: The caution under HEADSET AUDIO FAILURE explains that on aircraft where the low RPM horn is provided through the audio system, the pilot will not hear the horn when the headset has failed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: HEADSET AUDIO FAILURE (p.3-5)

items.question: According to the LOW RPM HORN audio alerts description, where is the horn audio provided on earlier versus later aircraft?
options: In the cabin ceiling on earlier aircraft and in the doors on later aircraft
Through speakers in the instrument console on earlier aircraft and through the audio system on later aircraft
Through the intercom on earlier aircraft and directly in the headset on later aircraft
Through the cabin speakers only on all aircraft
items.explanation: The LOW RPM HORN description states that the horn is provided by one or two speakers in the side of the instrument console on earlier aircraft, or through the audio system on later aircraft.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AUDIO ALERTS - LOW RPM HORN (p.3-11)

items.question: When does the LOW RPM horn activate and what does it indicate?
options: It activates at engine idle and indicates low oil temperature
It activates with the GOV OFF light and indicates governor failure
It activates simultaneously with the LOW RPM caution light and indicates rotor speed below 97% RPM
It activates with the ALT light and indicates low bus voltage
items.explanation: The LOW RPM HORN section explains that the horn activates simultaneously with the LOW RPM caution light and indicates rotor speed below 97% RPM.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AUDIO ALERTS - LOW RPM HORN (p.3-11)

items.question: Under what condition are the LOW RPM horn and caution light disabled according to the audio alerts section?
options: When airspeed is above Vne
When collective is full down
When the governor is switched OFF
When the helicopter is on the ground
items.explanation: The LOW RPM HORN description states that the horn and LOW RPM light are disabled when collective is full down.
references: R44 II POH Sec 3: AUDIO ALERTS - LOW RPM HORN (p.3-11)
